sources.title: Dossier scope and common assumptions
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: This fictional catalogue contains exactly three candidate methods: Slot Ledger (slot-ledger), Queue Repair (queue-repair), and Slot Ledger Private (private-ledger). Only Slot Ledger and Queue Repair model limited shared charger capacity. The private edition is a title distractor, not another shared-capacity method.

Both shared-capacity methods assume deterministic, known legs, travel times, energy use, tariffs and charger availability for the whole day. Both use 30-minute slots, require each charge to fit wholly inside a depot wait, and assume lossless charging at constant power bounded by the truck and charger ratings. These are modelling assumptions, not evidence about uncertain demand.

Every fictional timing below uses EVBench R1: one thread on the same illustrative reference CPU, including model construction and search until the first complete feasible daily plan passes coverage, sequence, charging, maintenance and state-of-charge checks. A solve need not prove optimality. The acceptance limit is at most 60 seconds; it is not a forecast for student hardware.

sources.title: Slot Ledger: shared-depot scheduling
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Slot Ledger (slot-ledger) is a mixed-integer daily-cost model. Binary truck-leg assignments and cancellations, deadhead links and charge-slot choices enforce coverage and the truck day. For each depot, charger type and slot, the sum of simultaneous charging trucks cannot exceed the available charger count. It therefore represents limited shared capacity, including separate slow and fast pools.

Slot Ledger uses the deterministic 30-minute, whole-wait, lossless constant-power assumptions in EV-S01:P02. It enforces truck and charger power bounds, maintenance exclusion, intermediate battery bounds and final home state of charge at least the initial level. It may optimise cost, but a time-limited feasible solution is not an optimality certificate.

sources.title: Queue Repair: shared-depot scheduling
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Queue Repair (queue-repair) fixes candidate truck routes for a repair pass, then allocates charging against a per-depot, per-type, per-slot occupancy ledger. A slot is usable only while its count is below the finite charger count. Conflicts move to another valid waiting slot or trigger leg cancellation and route rebuilding; an unresolved conflict is never returned as feasible.

Queue Repair assumes the same known deterministic inputs and 30-minute whole-wait, lossless constant-power charging as EV-S01:P02. It checks coverage, deadheads and return home, truck and charger power, maintenance, battery bounds and final state of charge after repair or cancellation. Fixed candidate routes and repair-or-cancel make this a feasible-plan heuristic, with no claim of global cost optimality.

sources.title: Slot Ledger: private-depot scheduling
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Slot Ledger Private (private-ledger) gives every truck its own always-available charger. It checks individual energy and charging power but has no depot occupancy sum. It does not model a finite shared charger pool; calling it Slot Ledger without the Private suffix confuses two different formulations.

sources.title: Slot Ledger: reference timing bulletin
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1
sources.reporting_relationship: initial experiment report; corrected by EV-S06

passages.quote: Initial fictional report EV-E-L1, family EV-F-L: Slot Ledger completed in 48 seconds on the 40-leg, 10-truck P01-shaped deterministic day. We initially labelled it eligible for shared chargers with a 60-second limit. This timing and eligibility statement is superseded by the dated correction EV-S06; keep this bulletin only to reconstruct the error.

sources.title: Correction: Slot Ledger reference timing
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1
sources.reporting_relationship: correction to EV-S05, not an independent experiment

passages.quote: Correction to EV-S05 and experiment EV-E-L1 (family EV-F-L): the 48-second run accidentally omitted shared charger occupancy constraints. Re-running the full Slot Ledger formulation with those constraints took 84 seconds under EVBench R1. Replace the 48-second time and the earlier eligible claim: Slot Ledger models shared capacity but is ineligible under the 60-second limit. Its capacity-modelling description in EV-S02 remains valid.

The corrected experiment retains identity EV-E-L1. The initial and corrected timings are two reports about this one experiment, not independent support. The correction changes the timing/eligibility conclusion, not Slot Ledger into the Private formulation.

sources.title: Queue Repair: reference timing bulletin
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Fictional experiment EV-E-Q1, family EV-F-Q, ran Queue Repair on a P01-shaped deterministic 40-leg, 10-truck day using shared finite slow and fast charger pools. Its complete feasible plan passed all EVBench R1 checks in 42 seconds, including charger occupancy. This supports eligibility under the 60-second limit for this tested setting, not optimality or a universal runtime guarantee.

sources.title: Queue Repair: reference timing digest
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1
sources.reporting_relationship: digest of EV-S07; no new run

passages.quote: This fictional digest repeats EV-S07 experiment EV-E-Q1 in family EV-F-Q: the shared-capacity feasible plan took 42 seconds under EVBench R1. No new run was performed. Do not count this document as an independent experiment.

sources.title: Queue Repair: reference timing slides
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1
sources.reporting_relationship: presentation of EV-S07; no new run

passages.quote: These fictional presentation notes reuse the same EV-E-Q1 result, family EV-F-Q, already reported in EV-S07 and EV-S08: 42 seconds with shared occupancy enforced. There are three documents but one experiment here; neither the digest nor these slides replicate the run.

sources.title: Queue Repair: second-day replication
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Fictional independent experiment EV-E-Q2, family EV-F-Q, used a second deterministic day with changed leg start times, still 40 legs and 10 trucks with the same finite shared charger counts and EVBench R1 timing procedure. Queue Repair produced a checked feasible plan in 55 seconds. This is a new run, unlike the EV-S08 digest and EV-S09 slides.

Queue Repair thus has two independent shared-charger experiments in this dossier: EV-E-Q1 and EV-E-Q2, both below 60 seconds. They share a method family, not an experiment identity. Two tested deterministic days do not establish reliability on arbitrary or uncertain future demand.

sources.title: Slot Ledger Private: fast reference timing
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: Fictional experiment EV-E-D1, family EV-F-D: Slot Ledger Private produced a plan in 8 seconds under EVBench R1 with a dedicated charger for each truck. The speed does not establish shared-pool feasibility. Private Ledger meets the time bound but fails the shared-charger requirement.

sources.title: Dossier boundary and decision scope
sources.provenance: Original fictional course dossier, issue #181, v1

passages.quote: All methods, authors, experiment results and timings in EV-S01 through EV-S12 are original fiction for this course, not findings attributed to a real paper. P01 supplies a scheduling problem only. There is no uncertain-demand experiment, numerical cost table or evidence of cost superiority in this A/B dossier.

For the tested shared-charger setting with a 60-second solve limit, recommend Queue Repair conditionally on the stated assumptions. Slot Ledger can represent the chargers but the corrected full solve is too slow; Private Ledger is fast but cannot represent their sharing. This is eligibility among the three documented methods, not a claim that Queue Repair is always fastest or cheapest.
